title: Clean replay of the historical Cicada 3301 OpenPGP artifact verification

target.description: Bundled historical Cicada 3301 OpenPGP public-key artifact

summary: The public verifier reproduced the recorded SHA-256 identity and both recorded OpenPGP fingerprints for the bundled historical key artifact.
why_run: To establish a byte-verifiable historical identity reference while preserving the boundary between artifact identity and present-day authority.

pipeline.description: Calculate the artifact SHA-256, parse primary and subkey fingerprints with GnuPG, then compare the ordered values with the public key manifest.

output.summary: SHA-256 and two OpenPGP fingerprints matched the public manifest.

acceptance.criterion: File digest and ordered fingerprint list exactly match the frozen manifest.

output.stdout: PASS — SHA-256 and 2 OpenPGP fingerprint(s) match the manifest.

controls: Reject a file-hash mismatch before fingerprint comparison.
Compare the ordered parsed fingerprint list with the declared manifest values.
interpretation: The bundled public-key bytes and recorded fingerprints are internally consistent and reproducible.
limitations: This is an artifact-identity reproduction, not a Liber Primus plaintext result.
A public-key fingerprint does not prove possession of the private key or present-day authority.
The intake history before the bundled bytes remains bounded by OBS-0001.

normalization_changes: Converted the flat public record into the canonical run-package schema.
No measured output or claim was altered.

raw_artifacts.reason: No separate historical stdout artifact was preserved; the exact recorded output remains in the canonical output object.
